# Findings: What GitHub Tells a Copilot Seat's Token

What was read on 2026-11-20 from GitHub with the Copilot token the app uses (`gh auth token`, stored by
`ds settings sync`), on the Linux machine with the **personal** seat (`individual_pro`). None of it is
documented by GitHub, so it can change without notice.

- **Seen** means it was in a real answer. **My reading** is what a field seems to mean from its name and
  its values: not confirmed by GitHub.
- **Not seen: a Copilot Business seat** (the work laptop). Its answers may lack fields, add others, or be
  refused by the organization's policy. Check there before relying on anything below.
- Identifying values (login, ids, organizations) are replaced by `<hidden>` in the examples.

## Summary

| Where | Request it costs | What it gives | Used by the app |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `GET https://api.github.com/copilot_internal/user` | 1, no credits | the plan, what the seat may use, its quotas (exact) and the reset day | title bar meter: app open and ⟳ (`ds.data.raw.copilot.copilot_usage`) |
| Headers of every model answer (`x-quota-snapshot-*`) | none of its own | the quotas again, as a percent left | the meter's fallback after an AI answer (`usage_from_headers`) |
| Body of every model answer (`copilot_usage`) | none of its own | what that answer cost, exactly, and the price of each kind of token | title bar meter after each AI answer; `credits` in the debug log (`ds.ai.model`) |
| `GET <Copilot API>/models` | 1, no credits | every model the seat lists, with limits and abilities | `experimental/copilot_agent/copilot_agent.py models` |
| `GET /users/<login>/settings/billing/...` | - | usage reports by model and day | no: refused for this token (see the end) |

### Who the seat is

| Field | Example | My reading |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `id`, `login` | | the GitHub account |
| `copilot_plan` | `individual_pro` | the plan. A business seat should say so here (not seen) |
| `access_type_sku` | `plus_monthly_subscriber_quota` | the product behind the plan (billing name) |
| `assigned_date` | a timestamp | when the seat was given |
| `organization_login_list`, `organization_list`, `enterprise_list` | `[]` | the organizations / enterprises that give the seat: empty for a personal one, expected filled on a business seat |
| `analytics_tracking_id` | | GitHub's telemetry id for the account |
| `is_staff` | `false` | a GitHub employee |
| `can_signup_for_limited`, `can_upgrade_plan` | `false`, `true` | upsell switches for GitHub's own clients |

### What the seat may use

All booleans, each a feature GitHub's clients switch on or off. On a business seat these are where an
organization's policy would show.

| Field | My reading |
| --- | --- |
| `chat_enabled` | Copilot Chat |
| `cli_enabled`, `cli_remote_control_enabled` | Copilot in the terminal, and driving it remotely |
| `is_mcp_enabled` | MCP servers in Copilot |
| `codex_agent_enabled` | the Codex coding agent |
| `copilot_app_enabled`, `copilot_app_office_plugins_enabled` | the Copilot app, and its Office plugins |
| `cloud_sessions_enabled`, `cloud_session_storage_enabled` | agent sessions in the cloud, and keeping them |
| `editor_preview_features_enabled` | preview features in editors |
| `copilotignore_enabled` | content exclusion (`.copilotignore`) |
| `restricted_telemetry`, `enterprise_usage_telemetry` | what telemetry is sent, and whether an enterprise sees usage |
| `te` | unknown (also a header on answers: `x-github-copilot-request-te`) |

### Where its requests go: `endpoints`

| Field | Example | My reading |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `api` | `https://api.individual.githubcopilot.com` | the model API for this seat's plan. The app uses pydantic-ai's default (`api.githubcopilot.com`), which answered too. A business seat likely names another host here (not seen) |
| `proxy` | | code completions |
| `telemetry`, `origin-tracker`, `exp` | | telemetry, and experiment flags |

### The quotas: `quota_snapshots`

Three quotas, each with the same fields. `premium_interactions` is the one that can run out: what the
title bar shows.

| Quota | What it counts (my reading) | On this seat |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `premium_interactions` | chat and agent requests to the models | 7,000 a month |
| `chat` | chat with the included models | unlimited |
| `completions` | inline code completions | unlimited |

| Field | Example (premium) | My reading |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `entitlement` | `7000` | the period's limit; `0` when unlimited |
| `quota_remaining` | `6960.0` | what is left, with part credits (it was `6977.3` earlier that day) |
| `remaining` | `6960` | the same, rounded down |
| `percent_remaining` | `99.4` | percent left, one decimal |
| `credits_used` | `39` | what was used, rounded down: 1 behind `entitlement - quota_remaining` (40), which is what VS Code shows |
| `unlimited` | `false` | no limit: then the counts are 0 and mean nothing |
| `has_quota` | `true` | the seat has this quota at all |
| `token_based_billing` | `true` | usage is counted in credits by tokens used, not 1 per request. Also at the top level. A seat still billed per request would say `false` and count requests (not seen) |
| `overage_permitted` | `false` | may go past the limit (paid) |
| `overage_count`, `overage_entitlement` | `0`, `0` | used past the limit, and how far past it may go |
| `quota_reset_at` | `0` | unused here; the day is `quota_reset_date` at the top level |
| `timestamp_utc` | `2026-11-20T16:33:44.514Z` | when GitHub made the snapshot: it can lag the latest request by some seconds |
| `quota_id` | `premium_interactions` | the quota's name |

Top level: `quota_reset_date` (`2026-12-01`) and `quota_reset_date_utc` say when every quota starts again.

**What it cost in practice (this seat, `gpt-5.6-luna`)**: a chat question to the smash agent moved the
figure by about 4.5 credits (35.5 to 40, seen by the user in VS Code); a bare "Say ok." by less than one.

## 2. The headers of every model answer

Each answer from the Copilot API (plain or streamed, seen on `/responses`) carries the quotas again, so
nothing has to be asked to know them after using the model:

```
x-quota-snapshot-premium_interactions: ent=7000&ov=0.0&ovPerm=false&rem=99.4&rst=2026-12-01T00%3A00%3A00Z
x-quota-snapshot-chat:                 ent=-1&ov=0.0&ovPerm=false&rem=100.0&rst=2026-12-01T00%3A00%3A00Z
x-quota-snapshot-completions:          ent=-1&ov=0.0&ovPerm=false&rem=100.0&rst=2026-12-01T00%3A00%3A00Z
x-quota-snapshot-cfi_overage:          ent=0&ov=0.0&ovPerm=false&rem=0.0&rst=2026-12-01T00%3A00%3A00Z
```

| Part | Example | My reading |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ent` | `7000` | the limit (`entitlement`); `-1` is unlimited |
| `rem` | `99.4` | **percent** left, one decimal (not a count) |
| `ov`, `ovPerm` | `0.0`, `false` | used past the limit, and whether that is allowed |
| `rst` | `2026-12-01T00:00:00Z` | when it resets (URL-encoded) |

- **Less exact than the endpoint**: a count worked out from `rem` is right only to a thousandth of the
  limit (7 of 7,000 credits). The app shows it as "about 42" until the next full read.
- **No plan and no unit** in the headers.
- `cfi_overage` is a fourth quota the endpoint doesn't list; unknown.

Other headers on an answer: `x-request-id`, `x-github-request-id`, `x-copilot-service-request-id` (ids to
quote to GitHub), `x-copilot-api-exp-assignment-context` (experiment flags), `x-github-backend`,
`x-github-edge-region`, `copilot-edits-session`, `x-reasoning-included`, `x-github-copilot-request-te`.

## 2b. The body of every model answer: what it cost

On this seat (token based billing) each answer ends with its own cost. In a plain answer it is a top-level
field; in a streamed one it is on the last event (`response.completed`), next to `response`:

```json
"copilot_usage": {
  "token_details": [
    { "token_type": "input",       "token_count": 9, "batch_size": 1000000, "cost_per_batch": 20000000000,  "model": "gpt-5.6-luna" },
    { "token_type": "cache_read",  "token_count": 0, "batch_size": 1000000, "cost_per_batch": 2000000000,   "model": "gpt-5.6-luna" },
    { "token_type": "cache_write", "token_count": 0, "batch_size": 1000000, "cost_per_batch": 25000000000,  "model": "gpt-5.6-luna" },
    { "token_type": "output",      "token_count": 5, "batch_size": 1000000, "cost_per_batch": 120000000000, "model": "gpt-5.6-luna" }
  ],
  "total_nano_aiu": 780000
}
```

| Field | My reading |
| --- | --- |
| `total_nano_aiu` | the answer's cost in billionths of an "AIU". **1 AIU is 1 credit of the premium quota**: measured, see below. Here 780,000 = 0.00078 credits |
| `token_details[].cost_per_batch` / `batch_size` | the model's price: nano AIU per million tokens of that kind. So `gpt-5.6-luna` is 20 credits per million input tokens, 2 cached, 25 cache write, 120 output |
| `token_details[].token_count` | the tokens of that kind this answer used (9 × 20 + 5 × 120 = 780 per million = the total) |

- **Measured (2026-11-20)**: the meter showed 41.2 credits used; one chat question in the app added its
  answers' `total_nano_aiu`, giving 41.3; GitHub's own count (`entitlement - quota_remaining`) read 41.3
  afterwards. One measurement, to a tenth of a credit.
- This is the only place a **price per model** shows: the model list no longer has one.
- pydantic-ai doesn't keep the field, so `ds.ai.model` reads it from the bytes as they pass (`_CostWatch`).
- Not seen on a seat without token based billing: there it may be missing.

### Prices of the models the work laptop offers

Read on 2026-11-20 from the `copilot_usage` of one tiny answer per model (personal seat; a business seat's
prices weren't seen). **Credits per million tokens.**

| Model | GitHub's category | Input | Cached input | Output | Against `gpt-6-luna` |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `gpt-6-luna` | lightweight | 10 | 1 | 50 | 1× |
| `gpt-5.6-luna` | lightweight | 20 | 2 | 120 | 2× |
| `gpt-6.1-terra` | versatile | 100 | 5 | 500 | 10× |
| `gpt-5.3-codex` | powerful | 175 | 17.5 | 1,400 | 18× in, 28× out |
| `gpt-6-sol` | powerful | 200 | 20 | 1,000 | 20× |
| `gpt-6.1-sol` | powerful | 200 | 10 | 1,000 | 20× (cached input half of `gpt-6-sol`) |
| `gpt-5.6-sol` | powerful | 400 | 40 | 2,000 | 40× |

- A newer model of the same family is cheaper than the older one.
- A typical chat question in the app (7.4k tokens in, half cached, 105 out) was 0.099 credits on
  `gpt-5.6-luna`: worked out from these prices, about 0.05 on `gpt-6-luna`, 0.4 on `gpt-6.1-terra`, 0.9 on
  the 6 / 6.1 Sol and on Codex, 1.8 on `gpt-5.6-sol`.
- `gpt-6-luna` reasoned a little on "Say ok." by default (11 reasoning tokens, billed as output); the
  others didn't.

### `gpt-5.6-luna` against `gpt-6-luna` on the app's smash agent

Three real questions each, 2026-11-20 (a small sample):

| Question | `gpt-5.6-luna` | `gpt-6-luna` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Jab 1 startup and damage | 4.0 s · 0.134 credits · 3 requests | 4.1 s · 0.065 credits · 3 requests |
| Which moves have armor, which frames | 8.3 s · 0.177 credits · 4 requests | 22.0 s · 0.386 credits · 9 requests |
| Forward tilt vs down tilt | 13.4 s · 0.279 credits · 3 requests | 13.3 s · 0.128 credits · 5 requests |
| Total | 0.59 credits | 0.58 credits |

- The facts matched on all three; `gpt-6-luna` was terser.
- `gpt-6-luna` made more tool calls, and on the armor question that cost more than its lower price saved.
- Reviews elsewhere (forums, third-party benchmark sites) read it as a price cut with a small quality dip,
  good for lookups and chat, weak for coding agents and long tool chains.
- The user chose `gpt-6-luna` as `DEFAULT_AI_MODEL` on this basis, then went back to `gpt-5.6-luna` the
  same day: pydantic-ai's bundled data (2.71.0, genai-prices 0.2.5) has no context window for `gpt-6-luna`,
  `gpt-6-sol` or `gpt-6.1-terra` on Copilot (the model list says 400,000), so the title bar's context meter
  lost its percent. The switch is a TODO next to the constant. Not tried: a lower reasoning effort to curb
  the extra tool calls.

## 3. The models: `GET <Copilot API>/models`

```bash
uv run experimental/copilot_agent/copilot_agent.py models
```

58 models on this seat. Each entry has `id`, `name`, `vendor`, `version`, `preview`,
`model_picker_enabled`, `model_picker_category`, `supported_endpoints`, `policy`, `capabilities`, and
sometimes `warning_message` / `warning_text`. One entry:

```json
{
  "id": "gpt-5.6-luna",
  "name": "GPT-5.6 Luna",
  "vendor": "OpenAI",
  "version": "gpt-5.6-luna",
  "preview": false,
  "model_picker_enabled": true,
  "model_picker_category": "lightweight",
  "supported_endpoints": ["/responses", "ws:/responses"],
  "policy": { "state": "enabled", "terms": "Enable access to the latest GPT-5.6 Luna model from OpenAI. ..." },
  "capabilities": {
    "family": "gpt-5.6-luna",
    "type": "chat",
    "tokenizer": "o200k_base",
    "limits": {
      "max_context_window_tokens": 328000,
      "max_prompt_tokens": 200000,
      "max_output_tokens": 128000,
      "vision": { "max_prompt_images": 1, "max_prompt_image_size": 3145728, "supported_media_types": ["image/jpeg", "image/png", "image/webp", "image/gif", "application/pdf"] }
    },
    "supports": {
      "streaming": true, "tool_calls": true, "parallel_tool_calls": true, "structured_outputs": true, "vision": true,
      "reasoning_effort": ["none", "low", "medium", "high", "xhigh", "max"]
    }
  },
  "warning_message": "Your billing plan has changed to usage-based billing and model multipliers no longer apply. ..."
}
```

| Field | My reading |
| --- | --- |
| `supported_endpoints` | which API serves the model: GPT ids only on `/responses`, the others on chat completions (`COPILOT_RESPONSES_PREFIXES` in `ds.ai.model`) |
| `policy.state` | `enabled`, or what the seat's owner still has to accept. **On a business seat this is where the organization's allowed models show** (not seen) |
| `capabilities.limits` | the context window, the largest prompt and answer, image limits |
| `capabilities.supports` | tools, structured output, vision, the reasoning efforts it takes |
| `model_picker_category` | how editors group it (`lightweight`, ...) |
| `warning_message` | says this seat moved to usage-based billing: there is **no price or multiplier per model** in the list any more |

## 4. What was asked for and not given

| Request | Answer | Why |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `GET /users/<login>/settings/billing/premium_request/usage` | 404 | GitHub's documented report of premium requests by model and day. Needs the `user` scope; the `gh` token has `repo`, `read:org`, `gist`, `admin:public_key` |
| `GET /users/<login>/settings/billing/usage` | 404 | the same, for all billed products |

- For a personal seat, `gh auth refresh -h github.com -s user` would likely open them (not tried: it widens
  the token).
- For a **business seat** the reports belong to the organization (`/organizations/<org>/settings/billing/...`)
  and need one of its admins or billing managers: not available from the laptop.
- So there is no cost per model, per day or per session for a seat's own token: only the running total
  above. That is why this branch has the title bar meter and no Spend tab.
